title: Non-deterministic crash in resource loading on game launch from editor
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproductible in 4.6.stable

### System information

Godot v4.6.stable (d68a0c4f0) - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 3 monitors - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9186) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-13900K (32 threads) - 63.71 GiB memory

### Issue description

I am loading a bunch of different resources on game launch using `ResourceLoader.load_threaded_request()` with `use_sub_threads == false`. Sometime when the game is launched from the editor, it crashes after the splash screen, leaving no error logs. When starting from scenes that end up issuing more calls to `load_threaded_request()`, the crash likelihood increases, up to ~70%. I have never seen it happen in the exported game.

Examining the data, near the crash site, each instance of the crash appears to be loading a different resource (e.g. a Curve or a .gdshader). This started around the same time that I noticed the error messages discussed in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/116551 . Although it may appear like an out of memory issue, there's definitely plenty of memory available, and the fact that it happens non-deterministically, and the successful cases don't use an unusual amount of memory suggests that that's a red herring.

If anyone can recommend further debugging steps, I'm happy to investigate the issue.

### Steps to reproduce

- Have a project which uses a lot of `ResourceLoader.load_threaded_request()`.
- Launch it from the editor.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

I was unable to reproduce the issue in a small project.
